title: People Ops — Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Guide
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary:

This guide documents Redwood Inference's standardized People Ops processes for hiring, employee onboarding, performance and feedback cycles, and practical manager guidance. It is intended for hiring managers, people-ops partners, and engineers who act as interviewers or people managers.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: Provide clear, repeatable steps to hire and onboard talent quickly and fairly, run consistent performance cycles, and equip managers with concrete practices to support career growth and team effectiveness.
- Scope: Applies to all full-time and fixed-term hires, and provides manager guidance for ICs and people managers across Engineering, Product, SRE, and Customer-facing teams.

Key SLAs and targets (People Ops commitments):
- Requisition approval turnaround: 3 business days from hiring manager submission.
- Offer turnaround: initial verbal offer within 48 hours of decision; written offer within 3 business days.
- Background check completion: target 5 business days (dependent on vendor).
- New hire onboarding completion (functional/role ramp): 30 days for ICs, 60 days for managers.

1) Hiring process (high-level)

Introduction: The hiring process balances speed and rigor to protect interview quality, candidate experience, and fairness. Roles: hiring manager (owns role definition and hiring decisions), recruiter (owns sourcing and offer process), interviewers (assess candidates to rubric), people-ops partner (policy, offer approval, compensation guidance).

Steps (numbered):
1. Role requisition and approval
   - Hiring manager creates a requisition in Greenhouse with role spec, level, salary band, and target timeline.
   - People-ops partner signs off on headcount and budget (SLA: 3 business days).
2. Sourcing and screening
   - Recruiter sources using inbound, referrals, and outreach; screens for minimum qualifications.
   - Initial phone screen (30 min) focuses on motivation, background fit, and basic technical/role fit.
3. Interview loop (standardized)
   - Interview loop design: 3–5 interviews depending on role (technical screen, system design or role-related assessment, ownership & culture fit, manager interview).
   - Use standardized rubrics (score 1–5) across dimensions: Technical skills, Problem solving, Role craft (domain knowledge), Collaboration & Communication, Ownership & Growth mindset.
   - Interviewer training: all interviewers must complete the interview training module and calibration annually.
4. Debrief and decision
   - Debrief within 48 hours of last onsite/loop interview. Hiring manager consolidates rubric scores and narrative, schedules a decision meeting with recruiter and people-ops.
5. Offer and negotiation
   - Recruiter coordinates with hiring manager and people-ops for compensation approval. Aim to extend verbal offer within 48 hours and written offer within 3 business days.
6. Background, references, and acceptance
   - Initiate background check on verbal acceptance. Finalize start date and GL account creation tasks.

Interviewer rubric (plain table)
Dimension | What to look for | Typical questions | Score guide
---|---|---|---
Technical skills | Depth of domain knowledge and correctness | Coding/design question, trade-offs | 1 (insufficient) – 5 (exceptional)
Problem solving | Structured approach, debugging | Clarify, propose, test, iterate | 1–5
Collaboration | Communicates clearly, takes feedback | Past collaboration examples | 1–5
Ownership & Impact | Proactively drives outcomes | Past ownership examples, metrics | 1–5
Culture add | Alignment with core values | Hypothetical behavioral questions | 1–5

Minimum interview fairness checklist (interviewers must confirm):
- Used the rubric and documented evidence for each score.
- Avoided illegal topics and bias triggers.
- Provided written feedback within 24 hours.

Offer approval matrix (summary):
- Up to band midpoint: hiring manager + recruiter approval.
- Between midpoint and band max: + people-ops compensation approval.
- Above band max: + VP-level approval and People Ops Director sign-off.

2) New hire onboarding (first 90 days)

Intro: Onboarding is a shared responsibility between people-ops, IT, hiring manager, and buddy. The goal is to make new hires productive, connected, and informed about company priorities and norms.

Pre-day 1 (owner: recruiter/people-ops)
- Send welcome packet (company handbook, first-week schedule).
- Initiate equipment order with eng-infra (laptop, dongles, access).
- Create accounts (Google Workspace, Slack, HRIS) and schedule orientation.

Day 1–5 (owner: hiring manager + buddy)
1. Day 1: Orientation (People Ops) — company values, benefits overview, security briefing (1.5 hours).
2. Role kickoff with manager: expectations, 30/60/90 goals, communication cadence.
3. Team intro and 1:1 scheduling (weekly for first 30 days).

First 30 days (owner: hiring manager) — Onboarding checklist (required):
- Complete role-specific training modules (list provided in LMS).
- Shadow teammates on core processes.
- First deliverable: small scoped task that touches the main stack.
- Schedule a 30-day check-in (manager + people-ops) to review ramp and blockers.

30–90 days (owner: manager)
- 60-day progress review: feedback on role competence, communication, and culture fit.
- 90-day performance checkpoint: determine status (on track, needs support, or PIP initiation).

Onboarding checklist (tabular view)\Task | Owner | Target day | Status notes
---|---:|---:|---
Equipment & access | Eng-infra/IT | Day 0–1 | Ensure access to repos, CI, dashboards
Security & policies training | People Ops | Day 1 | Complete security and privacy modules
Role training modules | Hiring manager | Day 1–30 | LMS assignments completed
First deliverable | Hiring manager | Day 15–30 | Small production-ready contribution
Buddy check-ins | Buddy | Weekly (4 weeks) | Cultural assimilation and quick questions

3) Performance & feedback cycles

Cadence and timelines:
- Continuous feedback: encouraged (1:1s, ad-hoc feedback)
- Formal cycles: Annual performance review (primary), Quarterly check-ins (recommended for fast-moving teams).
- Calibration meetings: Managers + leadership calibrate ratings within each function before awards and compensation changes.

Performance rating scale (short):
- Exceeds expectations (E): Consistently delivers high impact beyond role.
- Meets expectations (M): Solid, reliable contributor who meets goals.
- Needs improvement (N): Misses expectations; requires focused support.
- Unsatisfactory (U): Persistent underperformance; may trigger PIP.

Review workflow (bullet steps):
- Self assessment (employee) — due 2 weeks before manager review submission.
- Manager write-up — includes evidence and mapped rating.
- Peer feedback collection (optional) — anonymized, role-specific.
- Calibration meeting — final rating and comp recommendations locked.
- Feedback conversation — manager meets with direct report to deliver review, set next-cycle goals, and update career development plan.

Manager responsibilities in performance cycles:
- Maintain timely 1:1 cadence and document notes in the HRIS/Confluence.
- Provide regular, specific feedback with examples (both positive and corrective).
- Escalate concerns to people-ops early (if rating will be N or U).
- Participate in calibration and ensure equity across team.

Performance improvement (PIP) process (when needed):
1. Informal coaching: manager documents concerns, provides coaching and checkpoints (2–4 weeks).
2. Formal PIP initiation: if insufficient progress, manager works with people-ops to create a 30–90 day PIP with clear success metrics and check-ins.
3. Outcome: successful improvement and return to normal cycle, or termination if objectives are not met.

4) Manager guide: practical practices\n
1:1s and feedback:
- Cadence: weekly 1:1 for ICs and managers for first 90 days; at minimum bi-weekly thereafter.
- 1:1 template:
  - Quick personal check-in (5 min)
  - Blockers & priorities (10–15 min)
  - Career & growth coaching (10 min)
  - Action items and expectations (5 min)
- Note-taking: managers should capture high-level notes and actions in Confluence or HRIS; do not store sensitive personal data in open docs.

Career conversations:
- Discuss career aspirations annually and review progression criteria for next level.
- Use competency-level examples from the career ladder when documenting promotions.

Hiring manager interview responsibilities:
- Build an interview loop tailored to the role using standard rubrics.
- Ensure at least one bar-raiser or senior interviewer is present for IC hires at L4+.
- Provide timely feedback (within 24 hours) and complete rubric items with evidence.

Psychological safety & inclusion:
- Managers must prioritize inclusive interviewing and onboarding: diverse interview panels, accessible scheduling, and accommodation of reasonable needs.
- When conflict or harassment concerns arise, escalate immediately to people-ops and Security & Legal as appropriate.

5) Tools, artifacts, and links (operational)
- ATS: Greenhouse — requisitions, interview scheduling, offer letters.
- HRIS: Rippling — onboarding tasks, payroll, benefits enrollment.
- LMS: Docebo — training modules and interview training.
- Confluence: central source of truth for team docs, onboarding checklists, and career ladders.
- Slack: #new-hires, #people-ops for urgent coordination.

Checklist: Pre-boarding to 90-day quick reference
- Requisition approved (people-ops)
- Recruiter screens and schedules loop
- Offer extended and accepted
- Background check initiated
- Equipment & accounts provisioned
- Day-1 orientation completed
- 30/60/90 check-ins scheduled and documented

Escalations and ownership
- Offer delays (>5 business days) — escalate to Head of Talent.
- Background check exceptions — people-ops lead works with candidate and legal.
- Performance concerns at any stage — notify People Ops Partner within 5 business days.

Appendix A — Sample 30/60/90 template (manager fill-in)\- 30-day objectives: [Clear measurable tasks and learning goals]
- 60-day objectives: [Ownership of specific components, cross-team collaboration]
- 90-day objectives: [Lead a small project or feature, demonstrate measurable impact]

Appendix B — Interviewer training & calibration schedule\- New interviewers: complete training module before participating in loops.
- Calibration: quarterly (each function) with people-ops to align scoring and reduce bias.

Contacts

- Benefits & Payroll: payroll@redwood.ai
- Security & compliance: security@redwood.ai

Document maintenance
- Owner: People Ops (Maya Chen)
- Review cadence: annual or on major policy change.

This document is intended to be a practical playbook. If you have suggestions or need local team-level tailoring, contact your People Ops partner.
